CARES Cross-Document Architecture Consistency Review

Status: Documentation review only (NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT TESTED). This report records a bounded, evidence-based consistency review of inspected architecture documents. It does not implement application features, create database migrations, modify application source code, execute schema changes, or validate security controls.

1. Executive summary

Confirmed fact (from inspected documentation): The inspected documents consistently preserve the mandatory CARES constraints: Python backend, PostgreSQL as primary/authoritative relational system of record, external SaaS AI providers only with no local AI/GPU infrastructure, one unique monitored device equals exactly one licensed asset, multiple data sources reporting the same physical device must not create duplicate licensed assets, asset licensing separate from technical resource quotas, CARES core must operate independently of MELIRA, and no automatic provider/model failover. docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md, and docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md show substantial alignment on verified transaction-bound tenant context (not caller-controlled GUC authorization), protected evidence-transition authorization, explicit outbox replay/idempotency concerns, and stable binding/fingerprint-alias separation.

Technical interpretation: The documentation set is directionally converging but is not yet fully consistent for formal PostgreSQL schema design. The most important inconsistencies are: (1) docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md do not reflect the newer stable source-device binding model (source_device_key_id, source_device_fingerprint_alias) and transaction-bound trusted-context/evidence/outbox mechanics described in later documents; (2) role naming and privilege-boundary detail differ between DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md; (3) event-ingestion idempotency (event_receipt) and licensing/identity-operation idempotency are described in different scopes without one unified transaction-boundary model; and (4) several required technical and owner decisions remain open.

Recommendation: Resolve cross-document contradictions first by making docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md consistent with the latest approved technical direction (especially verified context, stable binding/alias identity model, role separation, evidence custody/authorization, and outbox/replay semantics) before formal PostgreSQL schema/security design review.

Unresolved assumption: This review assumes the current file contents inspected on 2026-11-21 are the intended latest working set. No repository version-control metadata (Git history/tags) was available or relied upon for document versions.

4. Confirmed consistent decisions

  1. Core platform and AI boundary

    • Confirmed fact: ARCHITECTURE.md §"Architectural principles" and system/deployment/MELIRA sections state Python primary backend, PostgreSQL required primary relational database, customer-selected external AI SaaS only, no local GPU, no silent/provider failover, and core/MELIRA optionality. DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Database decision and boundaries" states PostgreSQL is the required primary relational database and system of record. SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md states external SaaS AI providers only and no local AI/GPU infrastructure; MELIRA optional and not an authorization/autonomous action authority. FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §1 and ADR 0006 "Confirmed requirements (preserved)" preserve the same constraints.
    • Technical interpretation: The inspected documents agree on platform authority and AI boundary at the architectural principle level.
    • Recommendation: Preserve these statements as non-negotiable constraints in schema/security design.
    • Unresolved assumption: None identified for these constraints from inspected documents.

  2. One-device-one-license invariant and multi-source non-duplication

    • Confirmed fact: ARCHITECTURE.md states one unique monitored device is one licensed asset and identity resolution must not silently claim reliable deduplication/auto-merge on ambiguity. DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §§"Asset identity, deduplication, and licensing" and lifecycle/usage descriptions preserve one canonical asset per unique monitored device and multiple source bindings without duplicate licensed usage. SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Device, agent, and asset identity and licensing integrity" states the same. FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §1 and ADR 0006 "Problem"/"Confirmed requirements" preserve the mandatory commercial invariant.
    • Technical interpretation: The invariant is consistently treated as a core correctness requirement across all inspected documents.
    • Recommendation: Any schema/constraint design must encode this invariant through tenant-scoped uniqueness, transactional serialization, and auditable state transitions.
    • Unresolved assumption: Final identity-resolution authority/evidence standards and some lifecycle/quota semantics remain owner decisions.

  3. Asset licensing separate from technical resource quotas

    • Confirmed fact: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md distinguishes licensing/entitlement from quota/rate limits and performance/processing controls. SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md states "Asset licensing is separate from technical resource quotas" and quota/rate limiting is separate from licensing correctness. ADR 0006 explicitly preserves separation from technical resource quotas.
    • Technical interpretation: Documents consistently separate commercial/licensed asset accounting from technical capacity controls.
    • Recommendation: Maintain separate schema/entities/counters and policy enforcement paths for licensing vs technical quotas.
    • Unresolved assumption: Commercial billing treatment of reserved/pending/deactivated states is not decided.

  4. Custom GUC not an authorization boundary / verified transaction-bound context direction (latest security-aligned docs)

    • Confirmed fact: SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md states tenant authority must not be derived from user-settable custom GUC and describes signed tenant assertion verification, protected transaction-bound verified context, narrow trusted helpers, pool isolation/cleanup, and fail-closed behavior; it explicitly states "No custom GUC is an authorization boundary." FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §2 (Workstream A) provides detailed rationale, threat paths, preferred protected verifier-written transaction context, narrow SECURITY DEFINER helpers, ownership/privilege/search_path/cleanup guidance, and GUC-forgery prevention. ADR 0006 requires tenant-scoped authorization/verified context in merge/split and production-equivalent runtime roles in verification.
    • Technical interpretation: The most recent/corrected security and licensing documents are aligned that RLS/authorization decisions must rely on protected verified transaction context, not caller-settable GUC values.
    • Recommendation: Treat Workstream A and SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md as the authoritative direction and reconcile older/less-specific wording elsewhere.
    • Unresolved assumption: PostgreSQL version/mechanism for transaction binding, verifier implementation/cryptography/key custody, and exact role/grant model remain unresolved.

  5. Evidence integrity direction in latest security-aligned docs

    • Confirmed fact: SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md distinguishes operational/security audit records, forensic evidence metadata/objects, and append-only custody events; requires immutable evidence metadata, controlled transitions via protected transaction-bound authorization, append-only custody, evidence hash verification, tenant-scoped references, and states DB hash chain alone is not independently tamper-proof against privileged DB admins. FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §4 details immutable-field inventory with IS DISTINCT FROM, controlled procedures, direct update/delete prohibitions, security.evidence_transition_authorization single-use atomic transaction-bound mechanism, custody sequencing/hash chain, and purge/restore/reconciliation concepts.
    • Technical interpretation: Latest security/correction documents consistently reject GUC-based evidence-transition authorization and align on append-only custody plus controlled, atomic, transaction-bound transitions.
    • Recommendation: Use FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §4 and SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md as the baseline for any future evidence schema/security design; reconcile less-specific source docs.
    • Unresolved assumption: Storage backends, retention/legal-hold/purge approvals, external immutable/WORM controls, and operational procedures are unresolved owner/security decisions.

5. Contradictions and ambiguities, with exact document and section references

  1. Source-device identity model is not consistently decomposed across documents

    • Confirmed fact: docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Proposed logical data model" table defines asset_data_source as "tenant ID, asset ID, data_source_id, protected source-device key fingerprint and key-version, observed identity and link provenance" (table row at ~line 27 in inspected content) and states "A single data_source_id may have many source-device keys..." but does not define source_device_key_id or source_device_fingerprint_alias as separate entities. docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Tenant-isolated storage" states "Unique source-device binding on (tenant_id, data_source_id, protected_source_device_key_fingerprint) to one canonical asset..." (end-of-file inspected section). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §"Data ingestion and processing flow" and surrounding text describe identity resolution/source bindings at a high level without the stable-binding/alias separation. In contrast, docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md §"1. Stable source-device binding and fingerprint aliases..." explicitly separates asset_data_source, source_device_key_id, and source_device_fingerprint_alias, states fingerprint is not permanent identity, and defines alias overlap/rotation/lookup/collision/migration rules. docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Device, agent, and asset identity and licensing integrity" aligns with "asset_data_source and versioned fingerprint aliases" and states aliases are not permanent identity. docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §4.1 includes source_device_key_id as an immutable evidence linkage field example.
    • Technical interpretation: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md (and partially ARCHITECTURE.md) presents an older/simpler binding model that can be read as making fingerprint/key-version part of the binding record identity, while ADR 0006/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE/final corrections expect a stable binding plus versioned alias records. This creates ambiguity about the authoritative logical source of truth for source-device identity and rotation semantics.
    • Recommendation: High severity. Update DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md (logical model, constraints, lookup/rotation/migration narrative) and ARCHITECTURE.md (identity-resolution description) to explicitly align with ADR 0006’s separation of asset_data_source, source_device_key_id, and source_device_fingerprint_alias, while preserving existing invariants and owner decisions.
    • Unresolved assumption: Exact approved schema/constraint names, alias uniqueness tuple dimensions, and overlap duration/retirement policy remain unresolved.

  2. Verified tenant context mechanism is specified at different maturity levels

    • Confirmed fact: docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §§"Verified transaction context and tenant isolation" and "PostgreSQL privilege separation and RLS posture" specify signed assertion verification, protected transaction-bound verified context, narrow helpers, SET app.tenant_id/custom GUC not authorization, pool isolation/cleanup/fail-closed. docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §2 specifies the same direction in detail and states "Do not treat any custom PostgreSQL GUC as an authentication or authorization boundary." docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Tenant-isolated storage" states "RLS should use a transaction-local tenant context established by trusted backend code..." and describes access as application queries running under a limited runtime role but does not mention protected verifier-written records, signed assertions, or explicit prohibition of caller-settable GUC authorization. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md states tenant authorization at API/service and database boundaries but gives no mechanism.
    • Technical interpretation: The documents are not contradictory in intent, but DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md/ARCHITECTURE.md are underspecified and could be misread as permitting a simpler SET LOCAL/GUC-style tenant context if read without SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md and FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md.
    • Recommendation: High severity. Add explicit cross-references and mechanism-level language in DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md stating that tenant context must be verified and transaction-bound per SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md/FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md, and that custom GUCs are not authorization sources.
    • Unresolved assumption: Selected PostgreSQL transaction/binding mechanism, verifier cryptography, nonce/assertion lifecycle, and implementation details are unresolved.

  3. PostgreSQL runtime role naming and responsibilities are inconsistent/incomplete across docs

    • Confirmed fact: docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §"PostgreSQL privilege separation and RLS posture" defines logical roles cares_api_runtime, cares_ingest_runtime, cares_worker_runtime, cares_migration, and cares_maintenance with responsibilities and prohibitions (no SUPERUSER/BYPASSRLS/table ownership/security-function/policy ownership for ordinary runtime roles). docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Tenant-isolated storage" refers to "Runtime role" (singular) and "a migration role separate from the runtime application role." docs/ARCHITECTURE.md does not define DB roles. ADR 0006 verification requires "production-equivalent non-owner runtime roles" (plural concept implied). FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md discusses security-internal definer ownership/EXECUTE grants and role boundaries generally.
    • Technical interpretation: Security architecture has moved to a more granular least-privilege model, while data architecture still reflects a simpler role abstraction. This is an ambiguity that can affect future schema grants, RLS testing, and migration design.
    • Recommendation: High severity. Normalize role vocabulary in DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md (and add a brief note in ARCHITECTURE.md if appropriate) to the SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md logical role set or explicitly map "runtime role" to that set.
    • Unresolved assumption: Final grant matrices, definer owners, break-glass/admin model, and partition-child-table direct-access exceptions are unresolved owner/security decisions.

  4. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and RLS policy composition are not uniformly explicit

    • Confirmed fact: docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md states RLS is a mandatory second boundary, describes permissive gates/restrictive tenant boundary/action-scope model, and requires runtime roles to not bypass RLS; it does not explicitly state FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY in the inspected text. docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md states "RLS is a required defense in depth, not a substitute..." and mentions unique constraints/tenant ID in keys/indexes/checks but not FORCE RLS. docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §5 discusses RLS UPDATE/SELECT interaction and policy implications in detail. docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md requires RLS/security review and tenant isolation tests. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md states tenant authorization at DB boundary generally.
    • Technical interpretation: Intent is consistent that RLS is required and table ownership/bypass must be controlled, but explicit FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and per-command policy composition details are not consistently documented across source docs.
    • Recommendation: Medium severity. State FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (where applicable, subject to PostgreSQL/version/ownership review), table ownership, and policy-composition expectations consistently in DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md with cross-reference to final corrections/ADR.
    • Unresolved assumption: Exact tables requiring FORCE RLS, ownership model, and permissive/restrictive policy definitions remain to be designed/reviewed.

  5. Idempotency scope and ledger terminology differ (event ingestion vs licensing/identity operations)

    • Confirmed fact: docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Proposed logical data model" and §"PostgreSQL storage, partitioning, retention" define event_receipt as an unpartitioned/global idempotency guard for ingestion with unique (tenant_id, source_id, source_event_key), payload-hash comparison, and atomic insert with partitioned event row and outbox row. docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Tenant-isolated storage" states "Use an idempotency key for retried registration requests." docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md §5 defines a proposed durable, tenant-scoped idempotency persistence model/ledger for licensing/identity operations (operation type, request hash, result/reference, processing/completed/failed semantics, duplicates/conflicting payloads, retries after unknown commit/merge/split/lifecycle transitions). docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §3 defines outbox replay/attempt/generation idempotency semantics for external delivery/replay workflows.
    • Technical interpretation: The documents address different idempotency domains (event ingestion, licensing registration/identity operations, outbox delivery/replay) but do not present one unified taxonomy or transaction-boundary map. This can create ambiguity in schema design about required ledgers/tables and which operation must persist which result atomically.
    • Recommendation: High severity. Document a unified idempotency model distinguishing event_receipt (ingestion acceptance), licensing/identity operation ledger (ADR 0006), and outbox attempt/replay records (final corrections), including when each is written/committed relative to business state.
    • Unresolved assumption: Exact schema names, retention periods, result serialization, and operation coverage for the licensing/identity ledger are unresolved.

  6. Outbox semantics are detailed for delivery/replay in final corrections but not fully harmonized with ingestion/data-architecture descriptions

    • Confirmed fact: docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Worker concurrency, backpressure, retries, and dead letters" describes PostgreSQL transactional outbox, leases/recoverable claims, idempotent processing by (tenant_id, source_id, source_event_key), transient retries up to 10 attempts, terminal dead_letter, and authorized replay preserving original event/idempotency identity. docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §3 (Workstream B) proposes detailed semantics: cumulative attempt_count, unique attempt_number, replay_generation, per-generation max_attempts via generation-scoped counters, delivery_unknown safety state, reconciliation/authorization and duplicate_risk_accepted enforcement for ambiguous replay, preserved provider/request idempotency references, fenced leases/tokens, and explicit state transitions. docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md mentions transactional outbox for decoupling and authorization checks but not delivery-ambiguity/replay-generation mechanics.
    • Technical interpretation: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md describes a simpler event-processing outbox model; FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md adds materially stricter recovery/replay semantics (especially for ambiguous external delivery). It is ambiguous whether one outbox model applies to all event/identity/external-delivery workflows or whether separate outbox classes/tables are required.
    • Recommendation: Medium-High severity. Clarify in DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md which outbox semantics apply to event normalization/processing vs identity/external-provider side effects, and align with FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md where delivery_unknown/replay authorization is relevant.
    • Unresolved assumption: Provider reconciliation contracts, which workflows have external side effects, and exact replay authorization/owner policy are unresolved.

  7. Evidence/custody model specificity differs across documents

    • Confirmed fact: docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md provides aligned distinctions and controls for operational/security audit records, forensic evidence metadata/objects, and append-only custody events, including protected transaction-bound authorization and DB hash-chain limitation. docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §4 provides detailed immutable-field inventory, IS DISTINCT FROM trigger logic concept, security.evidence_transition_authorization mechanism, custody sequencing/concurrency controls, and purge/restore notes. docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Event and evidence lifecycle" and retention sections discuss evidence exports, authorization/access logging/redaction/integrity metadata, and possible future object store but do not specify custody-event append-only sequencing, controlled transition authorization mechanism, or immutable metadata field governance. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md does not detail evidence custody controls.
    • Technical interpretation: No direct conflict in stated goals, but there is a specificity/coverage gap: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md do not yet reflect the controlled-evidence-transition and custody model required by the latest security corrections.
    • Recommendation: Medium severity. Update DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md evidence/audit entities and lifecycle descriptions to align with SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md/FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md (immutable metadata, append-only custody events, controlled transitions, tenant-scoped evidence access, hash/provenance handling).
    • Unresolved assumption: Evidence storage architecture (DB/object store/WORM), retention/legal-hold implementation, and purge/restore procedures remain owner/security decisions.

  8. Licensing accounting detail is strongest in ADR 0006 but only partially mirrored elsewhere

    • Confirmed fact: docs/adr/0006-atomic-per-tenant-asset-licensing.md §2 defines separated measures (Active billable usage, Reserved capacity, Pending identity reservation, Available capacity, Historical/tombstone records), proposed equations, and state-to-counter mapping with owner decisions labeled. docs/DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md §"Tenant-isolated storage" states "Track separately: active billable monitored assets, temporarily reserved slots, pending identity reservations, and available quota" and proposes available = max(licensed_quota - active_assets - reserved_slots - pending_reservations, 0) and pending policy proposal under owner approval. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md mention licensing/quota/counters at higher level without the same formal mapping.
    • Technical interpretation: Directionally consistent but not fully harmonized in terminology and policy-mapping detail (e.g. "temporarily reserved slots"/reserved_slots vs reserved_capacity, billability of deactivated grace/reserved states explicitly left to owner decisions in ADR 0006 but described as proposal in DATA_ARCHITECTURE). Risk of divergent implementation interpretations exists.
    • Recommendation: Medium severity. Normalize accounting terminology and explicitly mark commercial/billing semantics as owner decisions in DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and any related summaries, using ADR 0006 as the technical reference model.
    • Unresolved assumption: Owner decisions listed in ADR 0006 §2 remain pending.

6. Missing technical decisions

  1. Identity model and schema formalization

    • Confirmed fact: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md still models fingerprint/key-version inside asset_data_source while ADR 0006 requires stable binding/alias separation. Final corrections include source_device_key_id in evidence context but does not define the full identity schema. (Refs: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md logical model/tenant-isolated storage; ADR 0006 §1; FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §4.1)
    • Technical interpretation: Missing a single reconciled, schema-ready logical definition of canonical asset, asset_data_source, source_device_key_id, source_device_fingerprint_alias, pending identity entities, and identity observation/resolution evidence.
    • Recommendation: Produce a reconciled identity/data-model decision before schema design.
    • Unresolved assumption: Which fields are authoritative, immutable, and tenant-keyed in each entity.

  2. Verified transaction context implementation details

    • Confirmed fact: SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md and FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §2 require protected, verifier-written, transaction-bound verified context and prohibit GUC authorization but leave mechanism selection open. FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §13 states PostgreSQL version, transaction/binding mechanism, verifier implementation, and role/grant model must be selected/validated.
    • Technical interpretation: The trust model is chosen in principle but not technically specified enough for schema/function design.
    • Recommendation: Decide binding identifiers/mechanism, verifier cryptography/format, nonce lifecycle, helper interfaces, and cleanup semantics.
    • Unresolved assumption: Availability of required PostgreSQL features/transaction identifiers and operational behavior under pooling.

  3. Unified idempotency and transaction-boundary map

    • Confirmed fact: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md defines event_receipt and outbox behavior; ADR 0006 defines a licensing/identity idempotency ledger; FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md defines outbox attempt/replay/generation semantics and atomic evidence authorization/update/custody/consume. (Refs cited above)
    • Technical interpretation: Missing an end-to-end map of which records/outcomes must commit atomically for registration, attachment, merge, split, deactivation/reactivation/removal, fingerprint rotation, evidence transitions, and external-delivery workflows, including unknown-commit reconciliation boundaries.
    • Recommendation: Define operation-by-operation transaction boundaries and idempotency/result-persistence rules before schema design.
    • Unresolved assumption: External side-effect boundaries and result reference formats.

  4. RLS/FORCE RLS policy catalog and role-grant matrix

    • Confirmed fact: SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md defines logical roles and policy posture; FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §5 identifies UPDATE/SELECT/RETURNING interaction; DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md is less specific. No document provides a concrete policy/catalog/grant matrix.
    • Technical interpretation: Missing concrete per-table/per-command RLS and privilege design required for formal PostgreSQL schema/security review.
    • Recommendation: Define FORCE RLS applicability, table ownership, grants, permissive/restrictive policies, and asset:write/asset:read behavior.
    • Unresolved assumption: Whether asset:write implies asset:read for row-addressed workflows (owner/security decision noted in FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §5).

  5. Evidence storage and controlled-transition operational design

    • Confirmed fact: SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md and FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md §4 define integrity/authorization principles but leave storage backends, retention/legal-hold/purge/restore, external tamper-evidence, and operational authorizations unresolved.
    • Technical interpretation: Evidence metadata/custody schema cannot be finalized without storage/retention/legal control decisions.
    • Recommendation: Resolve storage architecture and controlled procedure authorization/operational workflow decisions.
    • Unresolved assumption: Object store/WORM usage, immutable storage scope, and jurisdictional retention requirements.

  6. Outbox scope split and external delivery reconciliation contracts

    • Confirmed fact: DATA_ARCHITECTURE.md and FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md describe outbox/retry/replay at different specificity levels; FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md requires reconciliation evidence for delivery_unknown and provider idempotency handling.
    • Technical interpretation: Missing decision on whether event-processing outbox and external-side-effect outbox share schema/semantics, and what provider reconciliation evidence/contracts are required.
    • Recommendation: Define outbox classes, state machines, and provider/consumer contracts before schema design.
    • Unresolved assumption: Which integrations/providers support idempotency and what evidence proves outcomes.

7. Owner decisions that must remain pending

Recommendation: Track them as explicit decision records/inputs to schema design; document provisional assumptions separately where needed.

9. Explicit assessment of readiness for formal PostgreSQL schema design

Confirmed fact: Core constraints and several important technical directions are documented and partially aligned (notably in SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md, FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md, and ADR 0006). However, inspected source documents contain unresolved contradictions/ambiguities in identity model decomposition, tenant-context mechanism specificity, role model, idempotency/outbox scope, and evidence/audit data-model detail.

Technical interpretation: CARES is not yet ready for formal PostgreSQL schema design as a finalized, unambiguous cross-document baseline. It is close to readiness for a conditional/preparatory schema-design review only if schema work is explicitly bounded by: (a) ADR 0006 as the identity/licensing transaction reference, (b) SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md and FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md as the authoritative security/context/evidence/outbox correction references, and (c) a tracked list of required reconciliations and unresolved technical/owner decisions.

Recommendation: Do not treat the current document set as schema-ready without first applying the critical/high corrections in Section 8 (or recording approved superseding decisions). A formal PostgreSQL schema/security design pass may proceed in parallel only as a draft/proposal exercise clearly marked NOT IMPLEMENTED/NOT TESTED and contingent on resolving the identified ambiguities.

Unresolved assumption: Readiness may improve if there are approved decisions outside the inspected documents; none were evidenced in this review.
